query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the selective laser melting (SLM) process parameters can improve the dimensional precision and mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components while reducing fabrication-induced defects.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy (HEA) powder with a composition of AlCoCrFeNi
generation.intervention: Optimization of SLM process parameters, including laser power, scanning speed, and powder layer thickness
generation.conditions: Additive manufacturing using SLM, with a substrate material of H13 steel
generation.structural_mediator: Densification and microstructure formation during the SLM process
generation.mechanism: The optimized SLM process parameters can lead to improved densification, reduced porosity, and a more homogeneous microstructure, resulting in enhanced mechanical properties and reduced defects
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dimensional precision, increased mechanical integrity, and reduced fabrication-induced defects in the additively manufactured HEA components
generation.baseline: As-built HEA components with a relative density of 95% and a tensile strength of 800 MPa
generation.boundary: The optimized SLM process parameters are applicable to HEA components with complex geometries and can be used to fabricate parts with a maximum size of 100 mm × 100 mm × 50 mm
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the SLM process parameters and the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties is not fully understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: A designed experiment with a full factorial design, varying the SLM process parameters (laser power, scanning speed, and powder layer thickness) and measuring the resulting dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and defect density
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized SLM process parameters do not result in a significant improvement (p < 0.05) in dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and defect density compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified

AbstractThe equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy (HEA) possesses excellent properties including exceptional strength–ductility synergy, high corrosion resistance, and good thermal stability. Selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing facilitates the convenient fabrication of the CoCrFeNiMn HEA parts with complex geometries. Here, the SLM process optimization was conducted to achieve a high relative density of as-built CoCrFeNiMn HEA bulks. The mechanisms of process-induced defects and process control were elucidated. The microscale mechanical behaviors were analyzed through in situ scanning electron microscopy observation during the compression tests on micro-pillars of the as-built HEA. The stress–strain characteristics by repeated slip and mechanism of “dislocation avalanche” during the compression of micro-pillars were discussed. The high-cycle fatigue tests of the as-built HEA were performed. It was found that a large number of nano-twins were induced by the fatigue, causing a non-negligible cycle softening phenomenon.
